items.title: Why surface-level SEO tactics won’t build lasting AI search visibility
items.summary: Surface-level SEO tactics like schema, authorship signals, and branded concepts are criticized for lacking depth and offering only short-term gains in an AI-driven search landscape where LLMs prioritize knowledge graphs, expert entities, and trusted datasets. Brands must shift focus to structural changes, such as building internal AI infrastructure and entity-level knowledge management, to achieve sustainable visibility amid collapsing user journeys and zero-click environments. For SEO and content marketing, this implies moving beyond generic optimizations to foster genuine expertise and integrations that influence AI models, enhancing long-term authority and organic reach.

items.title: Google Discover Core Update Data: Local Publishers Lost Reach
items.summary: New data from DiscoverSnoop reveals that local publishers like Syracuse.com retained home-state audience reach but suffered significant national visibility losses after Google's February 2026 Discover core update, aligning with Google's emphasis on locally relevant content. Major publishers such as Yahoo, Fox properties, and Forbes experienced over 20% drops in article placements and audience scores, highlighting potential SEO challenges for national distribution strategies. This update underscores the importance of content marketing teams optimizing for hyper-local targeting to mitigate reach declines in broader feeds.

items.title: SEO vs AEO vs GEO: The Evolution Explained
items.summary: SEO expert Josh Nay outlines how traditional SEO focuses on keywords, content, backlinks, and technical tweaks for ranking in Google and Bing SERPs. AEO targets direct answers for AI chatbots and voice assistants, while GEO ensures visibility in AI-generated summaries from tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews through authority, uniqueness, and structured data. Brands must now run all three strategies parallel to remain competitive in the evolving search landscape.

items.title: 47% of Google Searches Show AI Answers First: GEO + AEO + Agentic SEO Strategy
items.summary: Digital marketing agency iTechSEO highlights that 47% of Google searches now feature AI answers first, urging adoption of GEO, AEO, and Agentic SEO to get cited. They share a full 90-day strategy guide for winning in AI search environments. This post emphasizes adapting content strategies for the AI-dominated search future.

items.title: SEO Evolving into GEO: Becoming Part of the AI Response
items.summary: Full Stack Marketer Tomas Corza argues SEO is evolving into Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) as search engines generate answers instead of lists. Success requires building topical authority, structured content, expertise, and optimization for AI inclusion rather than rankings. This marks a fundamental shift where visibility means being synthesized into AI responses across platforms like ChatGPT and Perplexity.

items.title: AWP 2026 Conference Tackles AI Ethical Issues in Publishing
items.summary: The Association of Writers & Writing Programs (AWP) 2026 conference is addressing the ethical concerns surrounding AI in writing and publishing. Discussions highlight problems like AI systems trained on pirated books and their significant carbon footprint. Sessions aim to guide writers on responsible AI use amid industry debates.

items.title: Publishers Weekly Announces Book Deals for Week of March 9, 2026
items.summary: Publishers Weekly details several major book deals from the week, including a debut novel about a queer poet amid marital strife acquired in a significant deal. Multi-book contracts span various genres, signaling active acquisition in the industry. These announcements reflect ongoing trends in publishing investments.

items.title: AI-Powered Scams Surge in Self-Publishing, Targeting Aspiring Authors
items.summary: A Guardian investigation reveals a boom in fraudsters using AI to scam self-publishers, exemplified by author Jon's heartbreaking experience with fake services. These scams exploit authors' dreams, supercharging deceptive practices in the indie space. Warnings urge vigilance in the growing self-publishing market.

items.title: Authors Protest AI Book Scraping with Empty Books at London Book Fair
items.summary: Thousands of authors released empty books titled 'Don't Steal This Book' at the London Book Fair to protest AI companies scraping content without permission. The stunt highlights growing backlash against AI training on copyrighted works. It went viral, sparking discussions on intellectual property in publishing.

items.title: Grammarly Introduces AI Agents Modeled After Authors Without Permission
items.summary: Grammarly has rolled out AI 'expert' agents based on real authors, including deceased ones like a historian who died recently, without obtaining permission. The feature offers writing feedback mimicking these authors' styles. Critics decry it as unauthorized use of authors' personas in AI tools.

items.title: BookTok Readers Demand First-Person POV, Reshaping Romance Publishing
items.summary: BookTok's romance community overwhelmingly prefers first-person narratives, rejecting traditional third-person styles and pressuring publishers to adapt. A Slate article explores how this trend influences what gets published in romantasy and beyond. Authors and houses are shifting to meet reader demands.

items.title: The Bride! Suffers Major Box Office Disappointment
items.summary: Maggie Gyllenhaal's 'The Bride!' opened to just $13.6 million worldwide against an $80-90 million budget, marking it as one of 2026's biggest flops. The film received middling reviews and low audience scores, with a puzzling release date contributing to poor turnout. It ended Warner Bros.' streak of nine No. 1 openings.

items.title: Pixar's 'Hoppers' Dominates Box Office with Record Opening
items.summary: Pixar's original animated film 'Hoppers' earned $88 million globally in its opening weekend, including $46 million domestically, securing the No. 1 spot. It boasts a 97% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes and strong audience reactions. The success ends Pixar's recent box office struggles for non-sequels.

items.title: Oscars 2026: 'Sinners' Success Sparks Debate on 'Wokeness'
items.summary: The success of 'Sinners' at the 2026 Oscars has led to discussions claiming it exemplifies 'wokeness,' though analysts argue it reflects quality over ideology. Post-2020 Academy changes aimed at diversity are scrutinized amid the film's awards haul. Viewers express mixed reactions to perceived shifts in Oscar voting.

items.title: Viral Post Lists Red Flags for Woke Content in TV and Movies
items.summary: User @SirBylHolte shares a detailed list of tropes like black characters in medieval Europe, incompetent male leads, and forced diversity that prompt him to stop watching shows. The March 5 post amassed over 12,000 likes and thousands of replies debating audience avoidance of preachy narratives. Many users shared similar experiences of turning off content.

items.title: 'Woke Bride' Bombs at Box Office, Crushed by Hoppers
items.summary: A March 9 X post highlights Hollywood's 'go woke, go broke' trend, citing the flop of 'Woke Bride' against Pixar's 'Hoppers' success. The conservative commentary points to ideology prioritizing over entertainment leading to poor performance. It links to analysis of recent box office results.

items.title: Satirical Meme Celebrates 'Woke is Back' with Oscars Sweep
items.summary: A viral March 9 post from @RANDOMC_L_EVENT humorously lists improbable events like 'Sinners Oscars sweep' and 'woke is back' in a video meme. It garnered over 5,000 likes amid ongoing debates on diversity in awards. Users engaged with jokes on Hollywood trends.

items.title: What small business owners are quietly building with AI while everyone else is “waiting to see”
items.summary: Small business owners without coding experience are developing practical AI tools tailored to their needs, such as an AI receptionist for a dentist office saving $4k/month on services, a demand prediction system for a food truck reducing waste by 40%, an AI photo editor for a wedding photographer cutting turnaround from weeks to days and doubling bookings, a churn predictor for a gym increasing retention by 22%, and a custom CRM for pest control replacing costly software. These examples demonstrate tangible impacts on efficiency and revenue. The divide between proactive builders and passive observers is widening into a survival gap.

items.title: Small businesses are the biggest AI opportunity nobody's talking about
items.summary: A team completed $200k in automation projects for a private equity firm, including AI-driven appointment reminders for a owned hairdresser, revealing the untapped potential in small business automation. This shift prompted a rethinking of the industry, emphasizing SMBs as prime targets for AI services. The post outlines a playbook for securing such high-value small business clients.

items.title: How AI is about to transform the C-suite for small businesses
items.summary: Mastercard is developing a 'Virtual C-Suite' comprising AI agents to deliver financial and operational expertise to small businesses, mimicking roles like CFO typically exclusive to large enterprises. This innovation aims to provide actionable insights and support for SMB decision-making. It represents a significant platform move to democratize executive-level tools.

items.title: How Small Businesses Use AI for Growth and Efficiency
items.summary: Small businesses are leveraging AI to automate repetitive tasks like busy work and emails, enabling 82% of owners to expand hiring rather than replace staff. This adoption is driving growth and operational efficiency without displacing workers. The article highlights real-world applications demonstrating AI's positive impact on SMB scalability.
